subtitle: Subnet Calculator, VLSM, CIDR
promotionalText: Quick subnet answers in the wiring closet, VLSM plans before the change window, and a VLAN table that catches overlaps before your switches do. Fully offline, free.
description:
VLAN Planner is a subnet calculator, VLSM designer, and route summarization toolkit built by a network engineer for daily use: the app you reach for in a wiring closet, halfway up a rack, or ten minutes before a change window opens.

Everything runs on the device. No account, no ads, no analytics, no network access needed. Free.

SUBNET CALCULATOR
- Accepts CIDR (10.1.20.0/22) or dotted mask (255.255.252.0)
- Network, broadcast, wildcard mask, first and last usable host, usable host count
- Correct /31 point-to-point (RFC 3021) and /32 host route handling
- Flags special ranges: RFC 1918 private, CGN (100.64.0.0/10), link-local, multicast, documentation blocks
- Binary view shows exactly where the prefix boundary falls
- Tap any row to copy it straight into your terminal or ticket

VLSM DESIGNER
- Enter a base block and the subnets you need with their host counts
- Allocates right-sized, properly aligned subnets largest-first, so nothing overlaps and nothing is wasted
- Shows utilization of the base block at a glance
- Export the whole plan as CSV for the change record or the IPAM import

ROUTE SUMMARIZATION
- Paste a list of CIDR prefixes and get the minimal exact covering set
- Merges only what actually merges: no over-summarization, so the aggregate never advertises space you do not own
- Useful for cleaning up route filters, ACLs, and prefix lists before you push them

VLAN PLAN
- Persistent per-site VLAN table: ID, name, subnet, gateway, purpose
- Live validation catches the mistakes we have all pushed at least once: duplicate VLAN IDs, reserved IDs (1, 1002-1005), overlapping subnets, gateways outside their own subnet
- Multiple sites, saved on the device, still there on the next visit
- Export as CSV

WHO IT IS FOR
Network and infrastructure engineers, NOC teams, and anyone studying for the CCNA who wants to check their subnetting work against a calculator that gets the edge cases right.

WHY OFFLINE
Because the moment you need a subnet answer is rarely the moment you have a laptop open and a signal. Basements, shielded plant floors, customer sites with no guest Wi-Fi: the app works the same in all of them, because it never needs a connection in the first place.

PRIVACY
No account. No sign-in. No analytics. No data collection. Your plans never leave your phone.
